To estimate the causal effect of graduating from high school on adult voter turnout, I will use an Instrumental Variables (IV) design. High school graduation is endogenous, as students more likely to graduate may also be more likely to vote regardless of the diploma. I will use the `credit_waiver` as the instrument, as it was randomly assigned and significantly increased the probability of graduation without affecting other aspects of the students' lives. The IV estimate will provide the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) for those "compliers" who graduated because of the credit waiver. The main threat to identification would be a violation of the exclusion restriction, specifically if the waiver influenced voter turnout through a channel other than increasing the likelihood of graduation.
